gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Noto Sans Bengali opens its mouths wide and keeps capitals low. Nippo, by contrast, is all wire-cut strokes with no pinched joints or flared ends, a display voice built for punch while the body just reads.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuki: Nippo leads with proud little lowercase letters bent like tubing, almost as tall as its capitals, and technical in feel. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki follows with rope-coiled, readable sans.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-brahmi: Flat, contrast-free letters cut like wire give Nippo its look. Noto Sans Brahmi follows with a high mean line and curves left open at the ends, so a long stretch of text moves along smoothly without snagging.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-buginese: Noto Sans Buginese reads like chalk arcs left unjoined, with short ascenders that keep lines low and quick to scan. Nippo adds a heading with no swelling in its bowls, which is the pair's sharpest edge.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Nippo builds its proud little lowercase from rounded rod, a single weight that looks cut from wire. And Noto Sans Buhid sits beneath it with generous gaps where curves meet stems, a high x-height giving the heading room to stand out.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-carian: Nippo stands tall in its small letters, with unshaded strokes of constant width that look cut from wire. And Noto Sans Carian carries on below with open scissor-blade terminals, so a longer passage feels clean and unhurried.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Approachable, first of all, thanks to the open s and c in the body. Noto Sans Chakma packs its lowercase up toward the caps while Nippo keeps its arches matched to its stems, and that tidy kinship is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-cham: Noto Sans Cham brings tall, rounded lowercase with open c shapes that invite the eye in. Nippo pushes every curve as thick as its stems, which gives the pair its strongest quality: distinct roles.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Noto Sans Cherokee sits as a tall band with short stalks. Nippo, wire-cut and proud in its small letters, reads like following a single thread, while the body's wide-gapped e keeps everything below it easy to follow.
gen-fs-nippo-gf-noto-sans-chorasmian: Curves that stop short instead of closing in give this body a breezy, open read. Noto Sans Chorasmian has a large x-height and short ascenders, while Nippo does the showy work with tubular strokes like bent copper pipe.
